questions.question:
24. Read the passage and answer the question.
Stephen Hawking was born in 1942 in an educated family. He is considered the greatest physicist after Einstein. As his reputation as a scientist soared higher and higher, fate followed with less rewarding things. Stephen gradually started losing control over the muscles of his body as he gradually became a victim of Lou Gehrig's disease. Since the age of thirty, he has been confined to a wheelchair with no power to control his body except for some limited movement of his head and hands only. He can speak only through a computer with a voice synthesizer that converts his messages into sound. But such a tremendous physical handicap has not managed to dishearten or slow him down. Stephen is still a relentless worker, using his computer to carry out research work as well as deliver lectures. He lives with his wife and three children, and he is provided with twenty-four hour nursing facilities by an American organization for his wellbeing.
How is he doing his work?
options: He is working with his wife and three children.
He is working with an American association.
He is working with a nurse for twenty-four hours.
He is working with the assistance of a computer and a machine that converts messages into sound.
He is working with research and lectures.
